items.title: India delays digital payments fee rollout amid retailer pushback

items.title: Amex introduces a framework to prevent AI agents from making unauthorized purchases
items.feed_excerpt: American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.

items.feed_excerpt: The steel industry is a big polluter, but Helix Carbon can upcycle pollution from blast furnaces to drive down emissions and improve margins.

items.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room
items.feed_excerpt: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."

items.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
items.feed_excerpt: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.

items.title: Cambridge Heavy Industries has been quietly building a desktop fusion device

items.feed_excerpt: Fusion power plants will need a lot of lithium, and Licube is preparing to be a key supplier.

items.title: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech’s most expensive mistakes
items.feed_excerpt: The San Francisco startup aims to help battery and chip manufacturers identify defects on production lines, reducing downtime and costly mistakes.

items.title: Rivian’s startup Mind Robotics hires former Ford EV chief Doug Field
items.feed_excerpt: Field also worked on Apple's secretive car project and oversaw development of the Tesla Model 3.

items.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm

items.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world

items.title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
items.feed_excerpt: The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.

items.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
